llm.summary: The midterm relief trade is mutating fast: yields fell again (10Y ~4.8%), the dollar softened, and gold broke to a two-week high above $4,100 — but underneath, the AI complex is being sold and the money is not going back into growth broadly. The most violent move on the tape is in AI-adjacent power: VST -13.8%, NRG -13.5%, CEG -6.7%, CRWV -9.9% pre-market, which says the market is now pricing political/regulatory risk to data-center power pricing under a Democratic Congress and hostile state politics, not just AI capex fatigue. Qualcomm fell 7-11% because a memory shortage is inflating device bills of material and crushing handset volumes — the first clean read that AI's component hoarding is now taxing consumer electronics, which matters directly to BBY. The Bank of England hiked to 4% and warned inflation nears 5%; Fed speakers (Hammack) are talking gradual hikes, and December hike odds sit at 77-81% — so the yield relief is political, not cyclical, and tomorrow's payrolls (~65K expected) is the pressure test. Regime trend keeps worsening: Stagflation 35.1 (+16.2 trend), Goldilocks 15.6 (-16.2), with Health Care 94, Staples 89 and Energy 88 dominating rotation against Technology -74 and Comm Services -73. The book's insurance/healthcare/defensive-value tilt remains exactly where capital is flowing, and today it gets a direct verdict: CAH and CI both report. One honest caution: Value's lead over Growth narrowed from 142 to 130 points, the first compression in days, so a short-cover bounce in the mega-cap complex can mute relative performance for a week without invalidating the rotation.

market_thesis.short_term: Index-level calm masking a violent internal rotation. The post-midterm squeeze already happened (best day since August); today's tape is AI and AI-power unwinding while gold, housing, travel and defensives bid. The binary is tomorrow's jobs report: a resilient print with pay still losing to prices revives December hike pricing, reverses the yield drop and squeezes gold and housing; a weak print extends the bull-steepener and keeps the 'everything but AI' rally going. The IPP/data-center power collapse (VST, NRG, CEG) is a new, unhedged risk vector for anything whose earnings depend on cheap, politically tolerated electrons — expect it to spread to grid and AI-landlord names before it is resolved. Banks turning cautious on lending in the Fed survey is the quiet negative nobody traded today.
market_thesis.medium_term: Stagflation 35.1 and Reflation 32.4 rising together with Goldilocks collapsing to 15.6 defines the next several months: sticky prices, central banks biased to hikes (BoE already moved, Fed talking gradual increases), and nominal growth that holds up just enough to prevent a dovish pivot. Fiscal gridlock plus tariff friction is mildly disinflationary on goods but removes the deficit-expansion bid; that caps the long end and supports long-duration Treasury flows. AI capex bifurcates further between the physical layer that is already contracted (semicap, interconnect, Nvidia's partner ecosystem) and the monetization layer that gets repriced (Qualcomm, cloud/software multiples, Palantir growth deceleration debate). Memory scarcity becomes a visible consumer price event in phones and PCs in 1H27. Earnings quality outside tech stays the best signal: Zimmer, AppLovin, Sabre, Novavax raised; Rheinmetall, Cummins, Gibraltar cut.
market_thesis.long_term: The binding constraint on AI is no longer chips but power, permits and local political consent — which structurally advantages regulated utilities, gas, nuclear, copper and grid hardware over fabless narratives, but only after the market finishes repricing who captures (versus who gets taxed on) that electricity. Supply chains keep duplicating: Nvidia policing cloud partners to block Chinese access, China blocking SoftBank-ABB, Europe reselling GPU access at 30-50% premiums — all of which embeds a permanently higher capex baseline and a higher inflation floor. Households spending more on food, housing and insurance entrenches a decade of bifurcation: value retail, generics and distribution, security-type products and healthcare delivery take share from undifferentiated discretionary. Humanoid robotics and agentic software become real capital sinks but, as Agility's IPO shows, the equity will be priced on losses for years.

short_term: Consumers are deferring phone and device upgrades as memory-driven BOM inflation raises prices — Qualcomm's handset slump is the demand signal, not just a mix issue.
Savers are chasing yield and inflation protection directly: I Bonds, TIPS and long-duration Treasuries are being discussed by retail at the same time gold trades above $4,100.
Households are re-engaging with housing and home improvement as mortgage proxies fall — housing stocks rallied on the yield dip, HD +3.3%, which flows to remodel/repair demand.
Travel demand is holding up and benefiting from cheaper crude: DAL +7.2%, ABNB gapping +5.6% into earnings, Sabre beating.
Businesses are tightening credit standards (Fed lending survey), which slows small-business hiring and capex before it slows consumption.

Enterprises are shifting IT budget to security and agent governance after €100mn bank hacks, blood-bank attacks and multi-agent AI intrusion campaigns; cybersecurity now outranks cloud and software in flows.
Retail attention is rotating back to crypto and to brokerage apps (Robinhood queries) even as institutional conditions tighten — an attention/price divergence, not a fundamental one.
long_term: Security — financial, physical and digital — becomes a recurring household and corporate budget line rather than an episodic purchase; insurance, custody and cybersecurity all compound.
Electricity moves from invisible utility to contested political good; consumers will vote on who pays for data-center load, reshaping where AI capacity can physically be built.

Healthcare shifts toward continuous monitoring, robotic procedures and distribution efficiency as the population ages — benefiting devices, diagnostics and the drug supply chain over episodic acute care.
Value-seeking becomes identity rather than necessity: after six months of pay losing to prices, trade-down behaviour in staples and value retail persists even if real wages recover.
Time and cognitive bandwidth are the scarce goods agentic AI is sold against; enterprises will pay for retrieval, context and workflow automation (Box/Nvidia) long before consumers pay for agents.
Physical labour scarcity pushes humanoid and task robotics from demo to deployment over the decade, with the economics landing first in logistics, assembly and surgery.
Mobility and housing preferences keep bending toward smaller urban units and multifunctional space, sustaining remodel and furnishing demand over new large-format construction.

what_changed_since_yesterday: Gold broke higher again — from reclaiming $4,000 yesterday to a two-week high above $4,100 today, with the dollar and yields both lower.
The 10-year fell further, from ~4.92% to ~4.8%, and December Fed hike odds are now explicitly quoted at 77-81% — a hike, not a cut, is the base case.
The Bank of England hiked to 4%, its first increase since 2023, and warned inflation will approach 5% — the first G7 central bank to actually move in this cycle.
A new and violent selloff in AI-adjacent merchant power: VST -13.8%, NRG -13.5%, CEG -6.7%, CRWV -9.9%. Yesterday's 'state-level backlash' risk became a sector-wide repricing overnight.
Qualcomm dropped 7-11% on weak guidance, with memory shortages explicitly blamed for suppressing smartphone sales — AI component scarcity is now visibly taxing consumer electronics.
The regime deteriorated further: Stagflation 35.1 from 34.4, Goldilocks 15.6 from 16.1, with trend readings of +16.2 and -16.2 respectively.
Value's lead over Growth narrowed to 130 points from 142 — the first compression in the rotation signal, worth monitoring as a possible trend break.
AppLovin delivered on yesterday's not-priced call, rallying 16% on a Q3 beat and strong guidance.
Rheinmetall plunged 17% on a second guidance cut from stalled military contracts — a direct negative for the defence modernization theme.
Agility Robotics became the first pure humanoid robot company to list, with losses prompting immediate scepticism; China blocked the $5.4bn SoftBank-ABB robotics deal.
Nvidia imposed new rules forcing cloud partners worldwide to restrict Chinese customers, after reports Moonshot AI sought Blackwell access in Europe at a 30-50% premium.
The Fed's lending survey showed banks turning cautious — a new credit-tightening signal that was not in yesterday's picture.
Energy earnings disappointed: COP -5.2%, EOG -5.2%, DVN -7.3% pre-market, even as Energy sector flows remain among the strongest at 88.
